instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.66 requires any person engaging in lobbying as a lobbyist to be licensed under §13.63 and authorized under §13.65, and §13.62(11) defines a lobbyist as one paid by a principal whose duties include lobbying, so all paid lobbyists must register.

Section 13.63(1)(a) provides that a lobbyist license expires on December 31 of each even-numbered year, and §13.64(2) similarly states principal registration expires on December 31 of each even-numbered year — i.e., biennial renewal (24 months).

Section 13.695(2) requires changes to information disclosed in the statement to be reported in writing within 10 days of the change; §13.64(3) similarly requires written notice before lobbying in a new area, but the 10-day rule is the explicit change-notification deadline in the chapter.

The lobbyist files a separate license application under §13.63(1)(a), the principal files a separate registration statement under §13.64(1), and §13.65 requires a separate written authorization linking each lobbyist to each principal — three distinct filings rather than a single combined form.
Section 13.63(1)(a) lists the required application contents (social security number, optional residence address, signature, and fee) and makes no mention of a photograph requirement.

Section 13.621(3) expressly exempts elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, and legislative employees acting in their official capacity from §§13.63, 13.64, 13.65, 13.68, and 13.695.

Section 13.621(2) provides that a state agency filing a statement under §13.695 (and its named officials) are not subject to §§13.625, 13.63, 13.64, 13.65, or 13.68 — i.e., agencies follow a separate, lighter reporting regime under §13.695 rather than the full lobbyist/principal regulations.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The Wisconsin statute imposes a 10-day deadline on the PRINCIPAL to file a registration after exceeding the $500 threshold (§13.64(1)), but does not specify a separate days-after-first-lobbying deadline for the lobbyist themselves. Under §13.65/§13.66, the lobbyist must be licensed and authorized BEFORE engaging in lobbying — there is no post-lobbying grace period for the lobbyist, so the question's framing (days after first lobbying) does not map cleanly onto the statute.
